label: copy-phase input digit 2 (fed-back 2, not the first token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the input token is the digit 2 (the model fed back its previous output of 2). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and never on any other input token. When the 2 is the first original token (recall_idx 1) it fires rarely and very weakly. Magnitude is largest when the 2 sits early in the sequence (original positions 1-3, i.e. recall_idx 2-4, top examples near max at orig position 2) and falls off for 2s later in the sequence. A repeated 2 directly after a 2 gets roughly half the activation. Misses that are inactive are mostly late-position 2s. Dev F1 0.94, mass recall 0.996.

issues: The test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.904, R 0.977, F1 0.939, mass recall 0.996. The phase and token claims also hold. The feature has zero activations in the original and delimiter phases, and zero on any input token other than 2. in_first is always 0 when it fires.

recall_idx 1 (the 2 is the first original token) fires on 9.6% of those steps and holds 0.4% of the mass. Every test-split miss is in this class and the activations are weak (0.01-0.22 of max). This matches the claim.

Precision is 1.0 at recall_idx 2-4 and 0.995 at 4. It drops to 0.83 at 5, 0.65 at 6, 0.71 at 7 and 0.82 at 8, so the false positives are late 2s, as the explanation says. I looked for a clean history rule behind the late-2 non-firing and found none. Digits among the previous four inputs, prev_tok being a digit or letter, to_go, L, in_count and n_digits all leave precision around 0.67-0.84. It looks like activations shrinking with position and falling below threshold, not a separate class of tokens.

Minor imprecision in 'peaks at original position 2'. The single strongest activations are at orig position 2 (recall_idx 3). By mass per active step, recall_idx 2 (orig position 1) and recall_idx 3 are about equal (0.371 vs 0.356 of the mass on 16.8k vs 16.4k active steps). 'Peaks at original positions 1-2' would be more accurate.

The 'a 2 directly after another 2 gets about half the activation' claim is consistent with the top examples (0.37-0.62 of max). Late repeated 2s often fall to 0 (e.g. 'i t k h 2 2', where the second 2 is inactive). Early ones still fire: precision is 1.0 for prev_tok==2 at recall_idx 2-4.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
